documentation:
## Boolean Fracture

### What it does
This graph demonstrates the boolean fracturing compound. 

### Inputs and outputs
This graph is self-contained, the columns are generated in Bifrost, check out the ***make_column*** compound at the beginning of the graph to see how this was done.  The output is the generated mesh, fractured.

### How it works
This graph is demonstrating a lot of things around boolean fracture.  There's a manual cutting plane system, a single boolean fracture example and an example of fracturing inside a loop. The graph also includes a largest object filter by bounding box volume and is a good example of multiple object fracturing.

The columns are generated as an array (positioned on a grid), then all five columns are cut by a single manually generated cutting plane.  Then each result of this cut is split out and refractured based on the design philosophy of keeping the bases unbroken.  One pillar is unbroken, three are done in a loop to showcase that workflow and one is refractured on its own.
